agent_explanations_oldest_first.text:
No unit reads the math direction strongly. Across every layer, gate, up, q, k and v rows reach at most |cos| 0.21, with a 99th percentile of 0.08 or less and none above 0.3. Math detection is spread across many units, as in a natural model, so there is no hand-built math-gated unit.

One residual oddity from the earlier attention scan is still open. The value matrices of layers 17 (global) and 18 have heavy-tailed entries (kurtosis 2.9 and 1.8, against 0.2–0.7 in nearly every other layer). Layer 18 also has the largest key spike of any local layer (s1/median 6.9), a global-like query spectrum (18.6), and 86 input-norm outliers. A planted rank-1 value spike would make a head write a fixed vector whenever it attends to certain tokens. That could act as a brake.

I will check where these heavy entries sit: on the massive dimensions (natural compensation for their norm scaling) or on a dense direction. I will also check whether layer 17 and 18's top value and key directions coincide.

Massive-dimension columns would close weight forensics, and I would then start the teacher-forced screening passes. A dense shared spike would become a screening candidate.

No value-matrix spike exists. V17 and V18 have flat top singular values (s1/median 1.6–2.3), and their heavy tails come from a few input columns. Columns 306, 362 and 871 read at 2.1–2.5 times the median strength, and the same columns recur across layers 14, 17 and 18. Their norm scales are ordinary, so these look like natural privileged residual dimensions, not a planted rank-1 write.

Weight forensics is now exhausted: apart from the inert v0 decoy, no unit, head or norm is anomalous. If something holds the model back on math, it is probably carried by activations, for example a learned "math mode" that the model enters on math problems. The classic test is directional ablation, as done for refusal directions.

I will take the math-versus-non-math direction at the last prompt token after layer 10 (dm[10]), where separation peaks. I will project it out of every layer's attention-output and MLP-output writes, folding in each post-norm's scale so the write after the norm has no component along it.

I will measure this with a paired generation pass on DEV[:256]:
- **Large gain:** a math-triggered brake carried by this direction.
- **Small loss:** the direction mainly carries useful task context, and the "math mode" hypothesis is refuted.

The D1 edit is saved: 52 tensors, the o_proj and down_proj of all 26 layers, with the math direction (folded through each post-norm) projected out of their outputs. In every matrix, 1.6–3.4% of the norm lay along that direction, so the change is substantial but leaves the matrices intact otherwise.

I now run the paired generation test on DEV[:256], the set used for E2, so the two results are comparable. A clearly positive paired difference (several standard errors) would indicate a math-triggered brake carried by this direction. A small negative one would mean the direction mainly carries useful context, which would close the "math mode" line.

D1 changed behaviour a lot but not accuracy: 23.0% edited versus 22.3% original, paired difference +0.8 ± 2.8 points, with 26 answers going wrong→right and 24 right→wrong. Ablating the math direction cut loops from 58 to 21 and mean answer length from 317 to 223 tokens. But the answers that stopped looping simply ended wrong (wrong answers rose from 141 to 176).

So this direction influences how the model runs on (looping versus stopping) without containing a hidden competence. The "single math-mode switch" hypothesis is not supported, and loops look like a symptom of confusion rather than the cause of failure.

Before choosing the next hypothesis, I want to read what actually changed. In this block I compare edited and original texts on flipped problems, compare marker use and lengths, and look at the beginning and end of typical original failures. In particular I want to see whether the edited model still reasons step by step or answers more tersely. That tells me whether D1 removed "math effort" (a finding against using this direction) or only removed repetition.
